newsitem.title: CHINA: Deng obituary backs Tiananmen Square crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Deng obituary backs Tiananmen Square crackdown.

text.p: China's official obituary of paramount leader Deng Xiaoping praised his decision to crack down on unrest in 1989, a warning to people not to repeat those ill-fated demonstrations for more democracy.

"Amid domestic and international political disturbances in late 1980s and early 1990s, the (Communist) Party and government, with the staunch and powerful support from comrade Deng Xiaoping and other veterans...maintained a clear-cut stand," the obituary said.

Western diplomats said the clear reference in the obituary to the 1989 student-led demonstrations for more democracy that were crushed by troops and tanks with heavy loss of life was intended as a warning.

"Thanks to the facts that the Party and government have kept a firm and sober-minded position and that the achievements of reform, opening-up and modernisation drive have taken root in the hearts of the people, we have stood severe tests... which makes the Chinese people happy," the obituary said.

China's communist leaders wanted to ensure that students, or workers discontented with unemployment and inflation, did not seize on the opportunity of Deng's death on Wednesday to take to the streets to voice their grievances, the diplomats said.

Beijing also wanted to avoid a reassessment of Deng or of the Tiananmen Square crackdown, diplomats said, an emotive issue among many Chinese who remain outraged at the violence Deng used to suppress the peaceful demonstrations on June 4, 1989.
"They're saying 'Don't think this is a chance to reopen that particular question'," said one Western diplomat.
"This is not a time for reassessing all that," he said.
He described the obituary as highly positive, with Deng's heirs not yet ready to question his achievements -- as Deng himself did after Chairman Mao Zedong died in 1976.
"They have not reached the 70:30 stage yet," the diplomat said, referring to Deng's verdict on Mao's ultra-leftist rule as 70 percent positive and 30 percent negative.
